title: Bioavailability of Amino acids from Acheta Domesticus
summary:
Proteine aus der Hausgrille: Top oder Flop für unseren Körper?   
In den letzten Jahren wurden vier essbare Insektenarten - darunter auch die Hausgrille 
(Acheta domesticus) - als neuartige Lebensmittel zugelassen. Sie gelten als nachhaltige alternative Proteinquelle.
Obwohl die Nährstoffprofile vieler Insektenarten intensiv untersucht wurden, gibt es bislang kaum Erkenntnisse zur Aufnahme, Verfügbarkeit und Wirksamkeit der Nährstoffe im Menschen. 
In der ProtinA-Studie erforschen wir daher, wie gut die in der Hausgrille enthaltenen Proteine für den Körper verfügbar sind und welchen Einfluss sie auf die Blutzucker-Regulation haben.
conditions: Serum amino acid profile over 240 minutes after ingestion of 40 g cricket protein or whey protein (dissolved in tomato juice or as a protein bar).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Healthy participants ≥ 18 years of age. Inclusion Criteria:
- Age
    Module A: 18-67 years
    Module B: 18-40 years
    male/female, balanced age and gender distribution
- BMI: within the normal range or overweight, but not obese (generally 18.5 to < 30 kg/m2)
- physically and mentally healthy
- Non-smokers
- A prerequisite for participation is sufficient language comprehension to fully grasp the content of the patient information and the consent form and to be able to make informed decisions.
- A prerequisite for participation is agreement to be informed about potential medical incidental findings.
Exclusion criteria:
- Strict vegetarianism / veganism
- Current weight loss diet / fasting or other special diet
- Regular intake of protein supplements (nutritional supplements) in the last 6 months
- Lactose, gluten intolerance or incompatibility
- Any allergies requiring medical treatment, especially against birch, dust mites, crustaceans, mollusks, milk, tomato, nuts, soy
- Participation in other intervention studies
- Irregular day-night rhythm (e.g., in shift work)
- Extreme athletes (male/female) (>2 hours of high-intensity sport per day)
- Pregnant or breastfeeding women
- Unstable thyroid dysfunction
- Diabetes mellitus
- Allergic asthma and bronchial asthma
- Acquired or hereditary blood clotting disorders
- Known liver or kidney diseases
- Heart attack or stroke in the past
- Consuming diseases and existing tumor disease within the last 2 years
- Unintended weight loss of more than 10% in the last 6 months
- Diseases of the gastrointestinal tract
- Bariatric surgery in the past
- No neurological, psychosomatic or psychiatric disorders except occasional headaches
- Regular medication: Exceptions: hormonal contraception, L-thyroxine
- Alcohol consumption >14 servings per week (One serving of alcohol corresponds to a glass of beer or wine. A glass of spirits counts as two glasses of beer.)
- Consumption of illegal drugs in the week before the experiment
